equivalence_model.story_stripped_kernel: Choose uniformly a word with n E steps and n N steps. Count indices k for which after 2k steps the counts are equal. Sum indicators for visits to (k,k); the visit probability is C(2k,k)C(2n-2k,n-k)/C(2n,n).
transformations_checked: city street route ↔ monotone lattice path
diagonal junction visit ↔ zero/return of a simple bridge at even time
expected visits ↔ local time / sum of visit indicators
equivalence_model.equivalence_notes: The wording 'visit' versus 'cross' does not matter for the MathOverflow answer cited below: the answer explicitly counts all (k,k) visits and says to subtract two endpoints if desired.

findings.relationship: For a uniformly chosen path from (0,0) to (n,n), an answer defines indicators for (k,k), sums C(2k,k)C(2(n-k),n-k), obtains 4^n/C(2n,n), and says to subtract 2 if endpoints are excluded.
